summary: 1932 Wisconsin Conservation Commission steel ladder tower in Price County: standing with lower ladder cut and cab glass gone; hike-only, no public climbing.

facts.design: Galvanized steel ladder tower, about 100 ft (30.5 m), on four concrete piers, with a seven-foot square steel cab and a caged exterior ladder

staffing.status: no longer staffed; last staffed season 1973 per Wikipedia and Forest Lookouts; nomination gives no final year

access.note: Public may walk to the tower on the original trail from the Wintergreen parking lot, but no public access to climb it. National Forest parking pass required.

visit.trail_note: Trail from the Wintergreen Parking Lot (crosses an ATV trail) to the tower; hike only, no public climbing

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest); Wisconsin DNR holds a special use permit for the site

events.note: Erected by the Wisconsin Conservation Commission under a special use permit on Forest Service land acquired in 1931; piers inscribed 1932
Forest Service took over operation; CCC Camp Riley Creek operated the tower for at least 1935 to 1941
National Register form gives 1957 as the end of the period of significance (1932-1957); not a staffing end date
Last staffed season per Wikipedia and Forest Lookouts; the nomination does not name a final staffed year
Bottom approximately 20 feet of ladder removed to meet fire tower safety standards
Added to the National Register of Historic Places in 2007 (Wikipedia gives July 3, 2007)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia and Forest Lookouts put the last staffed season at 1973; the National Register form gives 1957 as the end of its period of significance and does not name a final staffed year. The story reports both and does not pick one.

Only the NHLR page says the Forest Service restored the tower, with no date. The National Register form describes deterioration and missing elements, so the restoration is reported as the NHLR's claim and is not verified.

NHLR calls it an Aermotor tower. The nomination names the design as Wisconsin Standard Ladder Protected and says only that tower parts were listed from Aermotor. The story says the Conservation Commission built it and does not name a manufacturer.

notes_for_editor: Built date, design, cab, and CCC-era use rest on the NRHP registration form (dated August 2006, listed 2007) and agree with NHLR and Wikipedia. The end of staffing is disputed (1973 vs 1957 as period end) and is reported as disputed. The restoration claim comes only from NHLR, undated. Access is from Travel Wisconsin; no FS page for this tower was read. No rental info found. Two WebSearch queries via websearch.py; about six page reads plus the nomination PDF. The Wisconsin Historical Society record NR2273 and a Price County Review article about former Fifield lookouts appeared in search but were not read. The NRHP date is July 3, 2007 per Wikipedia while the form's Keeper line reads 7-1-07; the story says 2007 only.
